First packaged release. Claude Buddy puts a floating orb on screen for each
running Claude Code session, colored by what that session is doing — slate for
idle, violet while generating, amber when it's waiting on you — and clicking an
orb brings that session's terminal window to the front.

This is a beta. It works on the setups it's been tested on, but it leans on
platform automation that varies between terminals, multiplexers and Windows
configurations, so expect rough edges.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.1.0-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.1.0-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.1.0-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

Nothing else is needed — the .NET runtime is bundled.

`SHA256SUMS.txt` covers every file above. Verify a download with
`shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or
`Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Installing

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then double-click
**Install Claude Code Hooks.command**. Launch it from Applications; nothing
appears in the Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look for the icon in
the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. It installs per-user, so there's no UAC prompt.
Leave both checkboxes ticked to wire up the hooks and start at sign-in.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook that Claude Code runs. Until
that hook is in `~/.claude/settings.json`, the app starts and runs correctly and
shows **nothing at all** — which looks broken but isn't. The installers offer to
wire it up; let them. Your existing settings are backed up to
`settings.json.claudebuddy-backup` first, and re-running the hook installer
repairs rather than duplicating.

Hooks are read once when a session starts, so **restart any Claude Code sessions
you already have open** before expecting orbs.

If you run Claude Code in more than one place — native Windows, WSL, macOS —
each install has its own `settings.json` and needs wiring separately. See the
[README](https://github.com/wtvamp/Claude-Buddy#2-wire-up-claude-code).

## Known limitations

- **Windows installers are unsigned.** SmartScreen will warn; choose
  **More info → Run anyway**. The macOS builds are signed and notarized, so they
  open normally.
- **WSL + tmux together isn't covered.**
- Click-to-focus needs Automation permission on macOS, which macOS asks for the
  first time you click an orb.
- A session killed with Ctrl+C right at a permission prompt can leave its orb
  stuck on amber. Right-click → *Reset this session to idle* clears it.

## Building from source

Still fully supported and documented in the
[README](https://github.com/wtvamp/Claude-Buddy#1-install-it) — the installers
are an addition, not a replacement.
